Introduction[edit]

The best way to prepare for math contests is to do lots of practice problems and learn the material necessary to solve these problems. There are also many books and online handouts and lectures you can use to improve your problem-solving skills. Depending on your current abilities, you may want to start out with different practice problems, different books, and different areas of the forums. You should also try to strengthen the areas you are not as good at. This guide is intended to help you get started.

Disclaimer[edit]

If you're wondering whether you are ready for a certain book/contest, the best option for you is to just try it out. You don't have much to lose from trying it. Also, for any book, you have to do the harder problems, as well as the easier ones. Only in this way will you actually improve your abilities.

Overview[edit]

If you don't feel like going too deep and want a straightforward answer, here it is:

Beginner[edit]

To score well on middle school competitions (like Mathcounts and AMC 8), read the following AoPS books and take their AOPS Academy/Online classes simultaneously in this order:

  • Prealgebra
  • Introduction to Algebra
  • Competition Math for Middle School
  • Introduction to Counting & Probability
  • Introduction to Number Theory
  • Volume 1
  • Introduction to Geometry

Use AoPS's Alcumus tool constantly to practice all of these topics. When you answer problems incorrectly or take a long time to answer one, reread the part in the book that corresponds with that question. The more you do this, the better your skills will get.

Advanced[edit]

To score well on the high-school-level competitions (like AMC 10, AMC 12 and AIME), read the following AOPS books and take their AOPS Academy/Online classes simultaneously in this order:

  • Intermediate Algebra
  • Intermediate Counting and Probability
  • Volume 2
  • Precalculus

Use AoPS's Alcumus tool constantly to practice all of these topics. When you answer problems incorrectly or take a long time to answer one, reread the section in the book that corresponds with that question. The more you do this, the better your skills will get.

Online Resources[edit]

USAMO Guide[edit]

The USAMO Guide is a free, open-source, student-run platform for AMC/AIME/USAMO preparation, written by USA(J)MO medalists. Founded in 2026 by Pranav Ramesh, it aims to reduce the need for expensive private tutoring and paid prep courses by offering a free, structured, self-paced curriculum for olympiad preparation.

The Content is organized into four tiers that cover topics from complete beginner level all the way up to olympiad level:

  • Foundations (AMC 8)
  • Intermediate (AMC 10/12)
  • Advanced (AIME)
  • Olympiad (USA(J)MO)

Each topic within a tier comes with a curated list of external lessons, for students to quickly access explanations from different sources during preparation.

  • An extensive problem set spanning AMC 10/12, AIME, USAMO, and AoPS-sourced problems at a range of difficulties, with full solutions
  • A Contests subdomain hosting biweekly mock competitions to help students practice under timed conditions
  • A progress-tracking dashboard for logging completed lessons and problem sets
  • A Discord Community for asking questions and getting help from other students

Art of Problem Solving (AoPS)[edit]

Art of Problem Solving (AoPS) is an online platform for competition mathematics, founded in 2003 by Richard Rusczyk. It includes several components commonly used by contest students:

  • Alcumus, an adaptive practice system that generates problems by topic and tracks progress
  • Forums, where users discuss problems and post solutions, organized by competition and topic, including a High School Olympiads subforum
  • Contest Collections, an archive of past problems from the AMC, AIME, USAMO/USAJMO, and other competitions
  • For the Win! (FTW), a timed multiplayer practice game
  • AoPS Online School, paid live and self-paced courses covering prealgebra through olympiad-level material
  • AoPS Books, a series of textbooks at Introduction, Intermediate, and Advanced levels
  • AoPS Wiki, a community-maintained wiki for competition problems and information

Books[edit]

Art of Problem Solving Books[edit]

AoPS books are excellent resources to help prepare for math contests. They cover a broad range of topics, mostly focusing on Algebra, Geometry, Number theory, and Combinatorics.

  • Art of Problem Solving Introduction series and Volume 1 - Mathcounts, AMC 8, AMC 10
  • Art of Problem Solving Intermediate series and Volume 2 - AMC 10, AMC 12, AIME, USAMO

AoPS books break down specific areas of mathematics. These books are on 3 levels: Introductory, Intermediate, and Advanced. The Advanced series, as well as part of the Intermediate series, has not yet been published. These books are indexed here. Excerpts are provided, as well as pretests and posttests to see if the books are on the right level for you. A very important note is that the prealgebra series will cover topics from algebra, number theory, geometry, and counting & probability, but justs skims through the important parts. Theoretically, with extensive practice and going over the entire book multiple times, you could score well on the basic-level competitions like Mathcounts or AMC 8.

  • Prealgebra - Mathcounts, MOEMS, AMC 8
  • Introduction to Algebra - Mathcounts, AMC 8
  • Introduction to Number Theory - Mathcounts, AMC 8, AMC 10, AMC 12, AIME
  • Introduction to Geometry - Mathcounts, AMC 8, AMC 10, AMC 12, AIME, HMMT
  • Introduction to Counting & Probability - Mathcounts, AMC 8, AMC 10, AMC 12, AIME
  • Intermediate Algebra - AMC 10, AMC 12, AIME, USAMO, HMMT
  • Intermediate Counting & Probability - AMC 10, AMC 12, AIME, HMMT, USAMO
  • Precalculus - AMC 12, AIME, USAMO
  • Calculus - HMMT, Putnam

Other Books[edit]

Here are a few more books good for contests:

  • USAMO Guide, a free resource with lessons, a structured roadmap of topics, and practice problems for AMC 12 and AIME preparation
  • (Free) LambdaMath: Zero to 150: The AMC 10/12 Playbook (contains detailed concepts and problems) by Pranav Ramesh.
  • Art and Craft of Problem Solving by Paul Zeitz
  • Problem-Solving Strategies by Arthur Engel
  • Geometry Revisited by H.S.M. Coxeter & Samuel L. Greitzer
  • 102 Combinatorial Problems by Titu Andreescu & Zuming Feng
  • 103 Trigonometry Problems by Titu Andreescu & Zuming Feng
  • 104 Number Theory Problems by Titu Andreescu & Zuming Feng
  • Euclidean Geometry in Math Olympiads by Evan Chen
  • Ritvik Rustagi's ACE The AMC 10 and 12 book is a great resource to use for AMC 10 and AMC 12. The book has over 200 pages and contains 250+ problems with detailed solutions.
  • Free Mastering AMC 8 book is a good way to learn and review the topics on the AMC 8
  • Free Mastering AMC 10/12 book is a good way to learn and review the topics on the AMC 10/12

Other books can also be found online.

AMC 8[edit]

The following books are recommended for AMC 8:

  • Prerequisite for the other books: Prealgebra
  • Algebra: Introduction to Algebra
  • Geometry: Introduction to Geometry
  • Combinatorics: Introduction to Counting & Probability
  • General: Competition Math for Middle School
  • Number Theory: Introduction to Number Theory (Note: There is not much Number Theory on the AMC 8 except for in the final five problems.)

AMC 10[edit]

The following books are recommended for AMC 10:

  • Algebra: Intermediate Algebra
  • Geometry: Introduction to Geometry
  • Combinatorics: Introduction to Counting & Probability
  • Number Theory: Introduction to Number Theory
  • General: Volume 1

AMC 12[edit]

The following books are recommended for AMC 12:

  • Algebra: Intermediate Algebra
  • Geometry: Introduction to Geometry
  • Combinatorics: Intermediate Counting & Probability (review Introduction to Counting and Probability if needed)
  • Number Theory: Introduction to Number Theory (be sure that you are familiar with intermediate-level number theory topics as well)
  • General: Volume 2
  • Extra: Precalculus


For anyone preparing for AMC 8/10/12 or the AIME, USAMO Guide offers detailed tutorials and guides for every topic tested on these exams, along with a huge problem base and biweekly competitions to help you analyze your progress and practice staying calm under exam conditions.

For all AMCs, ivyleaguecenter.org has good mock tests (10/12). You can buy sets of 5, 10, 15, or 20 mock tests. You can also buy sets of 1, 5, 9, or 12 mock tests from Score150.

Many mock tests exist on AoPS (shown below) written by experienced problem solvers on the platform.

These will help you score well.

Practice Problems[edit]

Old practice problems and solutions sorted by contest and year are available on the AoPS Wiki and the forums. Here are some old contest archives that may be useful for practicing with:

  • AMC 8 Problems and Solutions - AMC 8 is a national contest for grades 8 and younger.
  • AMC 10 Problems and Solutions - AMC 10 is a national contest for grades 10 and younger.
  • AMC 12 Problems and Solutions - AMC 12 is a national contest for grades 12 and younger.
  • AIME Problems and Solutions - The American Invitational Mathematics Examination is a contest administered to those who qualify with a high score on the AMC 10 or AMC 12.
  • USAMO Problems and Solutions - The United States of America Mathematical Olympiad is a proof-based contest which is qualified for through a combination of AMC and AIME scores.
  • HMMT is a nice contest on a hard AIME level run by Harvard and MIT.
  • List of mathematics competitions.
  • User-Created Contests.

Strategies to qualify for the AIME and USA(J)MO[edit]

Qualifying from the AMC 12[edit]

Try to score at least 85 to qualify for AIME.

Qualification for the USAMO is much harder. Only 260-270 people qualify for each olympiad every year. USAMO qualifiers need a good AIME score. Try to score at least 11 on AIME.

Qualifying from the AMC 10[edit]

Try to score at least 100 to qualify for AIME.

Qualifications for the USAJMO is similar to that for the USAMO, except it only considers students who qualified for AIME from AMC 10 but not AMC 12. Try to score at leas t01 on AIME.

Forums[edit]

The forums are one of the best ways to find problems to solve, get help with problems you cannot solve, and collaborate with people of all levels and abilities. The forum is divided into many subforums for problems of different difficulties.

  • The Middle School forum is for Mathcounts and AMC 8-level problems.
  • The High School forum is a good place to find AMC 10/12-level and AIME-level problems.
  • The Contests and Programs forum is a good place to find problems from all the AMC levels, as well as the AIME and USA(J)MO.
  • The USAMO Guide Discord server, where you can get help with your doubts and join group problem-solving sessions with other students
  • The Olympiad forum is a forum for problems at the olympiad level.
  • The LaTeX and Asymptote forum is a place to get help with , which is what you use to type things like on the forums. It's also for Asymptote, which is what we use to make diagrams like this one:

Cheat Sheets[edit]

Many great reference guides are available for free on the internet.

  • (Free) LambdaMath: Zero to 150: The AMC 10/12 Playbook by Pranav Ramesh is a great resource to quickly revise all of the concepts/methods and formulas.
  • Ritvik Rustagi's 53-page long handout has all the formulas for the AMC 10 and AMC 12. The handout was made alongside a 4 hour long review seminar for AMC 10 and AMC 12. It's a great way to review and learn new topics for the AMC 10 and AMC 12.
  • BOGTRO's list of theory relevant to the AIME.
  • Sohil Rathi's The Book of Mathematical Formulas & Strategies is a great way to review all formulas on math contests like AMCs, AIME, MATHCOUNTS, etc
  • Coach Monk's MathCounts Playbook is a good place to start for MathCounts-level material.
  • Coach Monk's High School Playbook goes a little more in depth, and is useful for all levels of high school mathematics.
  • The Mandelbrot Competition maintains a nice list of topics you need to know for high school math competitions called All of Math in 3 Pages.
  • The Noah Sheets
  • The Popular Elementary Math Competitions Contests to build Math Interests
  • The Ultimate AMC 10/12 Strategy Guide: How to Qualify for AIME and USAMO provides a comprehensive guide on cutoff strategies, time allocation across question tiers, and key textbook chapters.
  • How to Stop Making Silly Mistakes on the AMC 10/12 provides actionable techniques to eliminate calculation slips, counting traps, and scantron errors.
  • AMC 10/12 Test Strategy: How to Destroy Anxiety and Outsmart "Troll" Problems outlines psychological tips for time management, solving with detachment, and dealing with deceptive early problems.
  • 15 Tricky "Curveball" Problems on the AMC 10/12 is a curated list of non-standard opening time-trap problems from recent AMC competitions.

  • Free AMC 8 Fundamentals Class: https://www.omegalearn.org/amc8-fundamentals
  • Free AMC 8 Advanced/Mathcounts Class: https://www.omegalearn.org/amc8-fundamentals
  • Free AMC 10/12 Class: https://www.omegalearn.org/amc10-12
  • Free AMC 8/10 Class: https://www.youtube.com/channel/UC-Nt9Uo03VSo2QTNIzsE_cA (Some special seminars occasionally with Olympiad Winners)
  • If you are serious about improving your problem-solving skills, AoPS offers several online classes, available here.
  • MathWOOT is an online class offered by AoPS for olympiad training. It has one of the best peer groups in the world and is a great way to prepare for the AIME and USA(J)MO.

Summer Camps[edit]

Summer programs are also a great way to improve problem-solving skills. Some of these include:

  • Ross Mathematics Program
  • PROMYS
  • Canada/USA MathCamp
  • MathPath (for middle schoolers only)
  • AwesomeMath
